subject: Harmonizing snapshot deletion windows & ColdStore subprocessor verification
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Joanna Patel <compliance@nimbushealth.com>, DPO Nimbus <dpo@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Harmonizing snapshot deletion windows & ColdStore subprocessor verification

Hi Joanna / Nimbus DPO team,

Thanks for the call earlier this week. As promised, I wanted to put proposed next steps in writing so we can align on a DPA amendment and the operational controls we need from any snapshot/archive subprocessor (ColdStore Labs). High level asks: 

- Proposed amendment language: allow a 90-day "snapshot grace window" for cold backups to support forensic holds and rollback. We are not proposing longer live retention for active content—this is strictly for cold snapshots and immutable tombstones.
- Subprocessor evidence: SOC 2 type II report (last 12 months), deletion API contract, and a one-page evidence checklist showing how long index/tombstone artifacts can remain in immutable backup.
- Escrow/restore process: an operational runbook for emergency data escrow restores and a comms SLA (24 hours initial response, 72 hours recovery estimate).
- Scope: EU data must be written to EU-only ColdStore buckets when the customer requires it. We will provide region routing policies.

ColdStore has told us they may retain snapshots for up to 120 days in their cold tier while tombstone markers exist for a separate 30-day reclamation window. That drives a mismatch with a 90-day request from some customers, so we need to settle on a single, auditable timeline we can write into DPA language and product behavior.

I've attached the current ColdStore subprocessor inventory and a draft DPA amendment proposing the 90-day grace wording. Can you confirm the minimum regulatory requirements Nimbus needs, and whether the 90-day window is acceptable? If not, what specific legal hold / e-discovery timelines should we reflect?

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync Monday to confirm requirements and call out any requested exceptions.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Head of Privacy & Compliance (Sales Support)
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: ColdStore_subprocessor_inventory.csv, proposed-dpa-amendment-90d.docx

From: Andrew Liu <legal@healthbridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Joanna Patel <compliance@nimbushealth.com>, DPO Nimbus <dpo@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Harmonizing snapshot deletion windows & ColdStore subprocessor verification

Marissa—

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple quick clarifying questions from our side before we lock language in: 

1) When you say "tombstone markers" remain in immutable backup, do you mean the deletion marker itself (metadata) or full records that are logically deleted? Our regulator cares about the ability to demonstrate physical destruction of deleted PII.

2) If ColdStore retains snapshots for 120 days, does Redwood have the ability to trigger immediate removal of a particular customer's snapshot outside of ColdStore's routine schedule (i.e., on a per-customer request / legal order)?

If the answer to (2) is no, we'll likely need a clause that ties the vendor to an expedited deletion process for regulated customers, or else specify a maximum allowed retention that matches our legal obligation.

Happy to jump on the Monday cadence if that helps.

Best,
Andrew Liu
Senior Counsel, Healthbridge
legal@healthbridge.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Andrew Liu <legal@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-11T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Harmonizing snapshot deletion windows & ColdStore subprocessor verification

Hi all—technical clarification from infra/risk side: 

- Tombstone markers: in our platform tombstones are small metadata records that indicate logical deletion; the underlying chunk data in ColdStore's cold tier may still exist until the next consolidation/compaction job. For cold snapshots we cannot guarantee zero-latency physical removal because ColdStore uses immutable snapshot blobs.

- Per-customer expedited remove: ColdStore has an API to trigger targeted snapshot deletion, but it is a manual process today and requires a signed request and an operational ticket with 24–72 hour turnaround depending on the tier. We are negotiating a guaranteed SLA as part of subprocessor onboarding; currently we can commit to a documented emergency delete path (we will surface the ticket id and audit trail in our Console).

Proposal to reconcile: Redwood will: 
  * Add explicit DPA language that ColdStore will execute expedited deletes for regulated customers within 72 hours of a valid Redwood-initiated request (and provide audit evidence).
  * Adopt a 90-day default cold snapshot retention in product, with an opt-in longer retention for customers who sign explicit exceptions.
  * For EU-only accounts we will require EU-region ColdStore buckets and include that as a subsection in the amendment.

Kimberly—can you confirm procurement is prepared to add the SLA and a contract appendix for ColdStore? Marissa—if Nimbus needs <72 hours we should capture that as a hard requirement in the DocuSign path.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Infrastructure & Risk
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Andrew Liu <legal@healthbridge.com>, Joanna Patel <compliance@nimbushealth.com>, DPO Nimbus <dpo@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Harmonizing snapshot deletion windows & ColdStore subprocessor verification — next steps

Andrew / Joanna—thanks for the quick turn. Next steps I propose based on Karthik's note: 

1) We will circulate an updated DPA amendment that:
   - Specifies a 90-day default cold snapshot retention;
   - Requires ColdStore to honor expedited deletes within 72 hours for regulated customers and produce an audit trail;
   - Includes a region clause for EU-only accounts.

2) Procurement will push an SLA appendix to ColdStore to bake the 72-hour expedited-delete commitment into their SOW. Kimberly is looping procurement.

3) Requested evidence: Marissa will upload ColdStore's SOC 2 report and the one-page deletion checklist to the HubSpot company record (link below). Please confirm whether the SOC 2 + deletion checklist satisfy Nimbus's needs or if you require additional artifacts (e.g., vendor attestation signed by their security officer).

Meeting: I've scheduled a 30-min stand-up for Monday 2026-09-15 10:00am PT to finalize amendment wording and sign-off paths. Calendar invite and DocuSign draft are attached.

HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890
DocuSign draft: https://docusign.com/link/abc123

If acceptable, we'll route the amendment through the DocuSign path and have procurement finalize the appendix with ColdStore.

Cheers,

Marissa Cole
Head of Privacy & Compliance (Sales Support)
Redwood Inference
